definition: Mona Talat Diab (Arabic: منى طلعت دياب) is an Egyptian-American computer science professor and director of Carnegie Mellon University's Language Technologies Institute.
details: Previously, she was a professor at George Washington University and a research scientist with Facebook AI. Her research focuses on natural language processing, computational linguistics, cross lingual/multilingual processing, computational socio-pragmatics, Arabic language processing, and applied machine learning.

explainer.lead: Mona Diab is an American computer scientist. Her work spans computational linguistics, natural language processing and responsible AI.

contributions.name: Diab is the founder and director of the GW NLP lab CARE4Lang.
In 2017 Diab joined Amazon AWS AI Deep Learning Group for Human Language Technologies, where she led the AWS Lex project for task oriented dialogue systems for enterprises.
Diab together with Nizar Habash and Owen Rambow, co-founded CADIM in 2005, a global reference point in Arabic dialect processing.

timeline.what: Master of Science, George Washington University
Doctor of Philosophy, University of Maryland
She was also a postdoctoral research scientist at Stanford University (2003–2005) under the mentorship of Dan Jurafsky, where she was a part of the Stanford NLP Group.
She served the computational linguistics community as elected member, secretary and president of ACL SIGLEX (2005–2016) and elected president of ACL SIGSemitic.
Diab served as an elected faculty senator at Columbia University for 6 years (2007–2012) and an elected faculty senator at GW (2013–2014).
